basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et cum audisset vocem Domini Dei deambulantis in paradiso ad auram post meridiem,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et cum audisset vocem Domini Dei deambulantis in paradiso ad auram post meridiem, abscondit se Adam et uxor ejus. Post meridiem tales jam convenerat visitari qui defecerant a luce veritatis. Unde apte Dominus meridie crucem ascendit, et promissa latroni habitatione paradisi, post meridiem, id est, hora nona spiritum tradidit; ut videlicet eadem hora qua primus homo lignum praevaricationis tetigerat, secundus homo lignum redemptionis ascenderet, et qua hora diei praevaricatores paradiso expulerat, ea confessorem in paradisum induceret.
